open_points.subject: calling principal for the deliverer flows
open_points.text: The kernel reaches it over HTTPS through the Portal's own front
open_points.question: Does the kernel itself execute the scan, deliver and record-publication calling flows, or does another owner-controlled flow call those operations while the kernel only provides reachability?
options: The kernel directly calls and coordinates all three operations
A separate owner-controlled agent or workflow coordinates them
The kernel calls some operations and another flow calls the rest
open_points.default_guess: The kernel directly calls and coordinates all three operations.

witness.initial: A confirmed project has one ready source photo and the deliverer is reachable through the Portal front.
events: The owner initiates delivery work in the workplace.
An implementer must choose which component calls scan, deliver and record-publication.
outcomes: The kernel sends and sequences all three authenticated requests.
A separate owner-controlled agent sends and sequences the requests while the kernel merely exposes or relays access.
witness.observer: The owner and operators inspecting request identity, logs and failures

open_points.subject: relationship between the R0-16 credential and the A5 token
open_points.question: Is this credential exactly the bearer token defined by A5, or is it an additional credential used between the kernel and the Portal front?
options: It is the A5 bearer token and there is no additional credential
It is a separate front-door credential in addition to the A5 bearer token
The Portal front authenticates the credential and injects or substitutes the A5 bearer token
open_points.default_guess: It is exactly the A5 bearer token.

witness.initial: The route is installed and the deliverer has loaded its A5 token.
events: The kernel sends a request through the Portal front using what deployment calls the deliverer's credential.
The front and deliverer authenticate the request.
outcomes: One bearer token authenticates the request end to end.
The front requires one credential and the deliverer requires a second bearer token.
witness.observer: The deployer configuring secrets and the kernel handling authentication failures

open_points.subject: OSV deployment check
open_points.text: The check of rule 2 is built: it is the deployment route of this service, as it is the Client Portal's.
open_points.question: Which module offers the operation that checks every installed distribution against the accepted OSV snapshot, and which actor invokes it before deployment?
options: A shared Client Portal deployment module performs the check for both images
A deliverer-specific deployment module performs the check
An external image-scanning service performs the check and reports its result to the deployment route
open_points.default_guess: A shared deployment-pipeline module invokes an external OSV scanner before accepting the deliverer image.

witness.initial: A candidate deliverer image has been built with its resolved distributions.
events: A deployment actor submits the image for release.
The deployment route must perform the rule-2 vulnerability check before accepting it.
outcomes: The existing Client Portal deployment module scans and gates the image.
A separate deliverer deployment module scans and gates the image.
witness.observer: The deployer locating the gate, its configuration and its failure report
